newsitem.title: USA: Second NASD examiner charging bias, inaction.
newsitem.headline: Second NASD examiner charging bias, inaction.

text.p: A second former compliance examiner is expected to file a $20 million dollar lawsuit against NASD Monday for discriminating against minority employees and not prosecuting some securities law violators, lawyers for the examiner said.

The action by Massood Gilani, a senior examiner in the National Association of Securities Dealers District 10 office in New York City until last fall, comes on the heels of another $20 million damages suit filed Sept 4 by Theresa Carr against NASD and a top District 10 official.

Carr said NASD forced her to resign because of her aggressive probe of "pay-to-play" in the municipal bond market. "Pay-to-play" occurs when dealers or other bond professionals give political contributions to state and local officials in exchange for bond business.

Gilani, a 57-year-old Iranian who became a U.S. citizen earlier this year, will allege in a 38-page complaint this morning that NASD discriminates against minorities in hiring, promotion and pay, according to a draft complaint obtained by Reuters.
He also will charge that NASD ignored his recommendations to prosecute certain brokers for "egregious" misconduct, says the complaint prepared by the lawfirm Singer Zamansky in New York City.

NASD, for instance, "engaged in foot dragging" when Gilani pushed officials to bring charges against Hanover Sterling & Co., a brokerage firm that closed down in February 1995, the draft complaint says.
The firm's problems cost investors "significant sums of money" and led to closure of, Adler Coleman & Co., the brokerage company's clearing firm, the draft complaint says.
An NASD spokesman said Gilani's bias charges are unfounded.

"Our employment figures speak for themselves," he said. "We are committed to a diverse and talented workforce. In New York, 44 percent of our workforce are minorities. Forty-six percent are female. Twenty-two percent of the managers in New York are minorities."

As for charges that NASD is excusing securities law violators, the spokesman said, "Gilani seems to have based his case on a few instances which we intend to look into further and respond to in court."
The complaint is expected to be filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of New York.
Gilani also will charge that NASD has a "single complaint policy," a system under which it routinely refuses to bring charges when there is only one complaint filed against a broker.
Gilani's lawyers also will announce today they plan to file another lawsuit in the next few weeks against NASD on behalf of a former NASD committee member.
